reason: Measured on the real page, every number in the problem statement holds. At 390x844 the owner surface renders bar 164 + horizon 269 + head 31 + a 288px bare lead-in, so the first moment's copy lands at y870 on an 844px screen and the whole first screen of a 2363px page is chrome and empty rule; the head is 62px wide with white-space:normal (b.css 113-124) so 'days away' does wrap to two lines at 31px; and .b-barActs at 390 is a 2-col grid with the primary spanning 1/-1, costing 78px over two rows. In the 1000-1279 band it is single column with the first moment at y890 on a 900px screen. SCALE.owner is a flat 18 at every viewport width (render-b.js:32, read once at render-b.js:93) while the other entries are per-medium, so the owner surface never takes a page-size decision. None of this is asserted by either gate. The core call - the owner measure should scale with width the way the brief scales every other medium - is right. The fix as written is not, and the specific check asked for is the reason: an owner row is 74px of copy at 390 and place() separates rows by copy height + 10, so 12px/day gives 84px against 84px needed. It clears with exactly zero slack, and only in the 390-700 band. At 360 the title wraps and the row is 96px, so 12 collides by 22px before the owner has touched anything. Worse, the proposed breakpoint is wrong: the desk type step is at 701px, not 1024, so from 701 to 1023 the row is already 83px and 12px/day collides by 9px - the rule breaks inside its own band. The barActs sub-fix also makes the composition worse, so the finding is confirmed with a sharpened fix rather than as written.
sharpenedFix: Keep the width-dependent owner scale, but key it to the row height and to the real breakpoint, not to 1024. Two acceptable forms. (a) Constants at the existing breakpoint: SCALE.owner = 14 below 701 and 18 at 701 and up. 14 clears the 74px phone row with 14px of air and survives one extra wrapped line to 88px; it drops the lead-in from 288 to 224 and the page from 2363 to about 1855, putting the first moment at y806 - on the first screen at 390. Never 12 below 1024: rows are 83px from 701 up and it collides by 9px there. (b) Better, and the version that survives real titles: derive the scale after first paint from the measure itself - px = clamp(12, ceil((tallest .b-copy height + 10) / tightest gap in days), 18) - written into data-px before place() runs, so the tightest pair always clears whatever the copy does and the proportion between one gap and the next is still one scale for the whole measure. Keep the '.b-measureHead { width: auto; white-space: nowrap }' below 701; it is a real 16px win and unwinds the wrap. DROP the '.b-barActs { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) }' clause: at 346px each action gets 110px, 'Add a moment' wraps to two lines so the row is 56px not 44px against the current 78px, and it demotes Publish from a full-width primary to a cramped equal third. If the bar's 164px is to be attacked, attack the wordmark block above the actions, not the action grid.
